QF.id: Clubbing, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses_25

question.text: Mr. Rahul has the following brought-forward losses and current year incomes in FY 2025-26: Brought-forward non-speculative business loss (FY 2020-21): Rs.3,00,000; Brought-forward unabsorbed depreciation (FY 2018-19): Rs.1,50,000; Current year business income: Rs.4,00,000; Current year rental income: Rs.1,00,000. In what order should the set-offs be applied, and what is the final taxable income?

answer.text: Set off unabsorbed depreciation first as it is older; taxable income = Rs.1,50,000

First set off brought-forward business loss Rs.3,00,000 against business income Rs.4,00,000 (balance Rs.1,00,000); then set off unabsorbed depreciation Rs.1,50,000 against remaining Rs.1,00,000 business income + Rs.1,00,000 rental income; taxable income = Rs.50,000
Both losses set off only against business income; taxable income = Rs.1,00,000 (rental income untouched)
Business loss lapsed as it is from FY 2020-21 (beyond 8 years); only depreciation set off; taxable income = Rs.3,50,000

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the Income-tax Act, brought-forward non-speculative business loss can generally be carried forward for eight assessment years and set off against business income in those subsequent years. Unabsorbed depreciation can be carried forward indefinitely and is permitted to be set off against income under any head except salary. As a practical ordering, brought-forward business loss is applied first against current-year business income, and only after that is unabsorbed depreciation applied against any remaining income (other than salary). For Rahul, the FY 2020-21 business loss of Rs.3,00,000 is set off against current business income of Rs.4,00,000, leaving Rs.1,00,000 of business income. Unabsorbed depreciation of Rs.1,50,000 is then set off against the remaining business income of Rs.1,00,000 plus rental income of Rs.1,00,000, fully absorbing the depreciation. Final taxable income = Rs.2,00,000 minus Rs.1,50,000 = Rs.50,000. The Trap: Prioritising unabsorbed depreciation over brought-forward business loss simply because it is older is incorrect; the conventional ordering is to use specific business losses first. Restricting unabsorbed depreciation only to business income ignores the fact that it can be set off against income under most heads (other than salary). Treating the FY 2020-21 loss as time-barred misreads the eight-year carry-forward window applicable to non-speculative business losses. Note: The cited workbook chapter supports the separate carry-forward and set-off rules for non-speculative business loss (eight-year carry forward, set off against business income) and unabsorbed depreciation (indefinite carry forward, set off against any income except salary). The explicit ordering rule — that brought-forward business loss must be set off before unabsorbed depreciation — is not spelled out in the cited pages. The framing above reflects the general Income-tax Act practice rather than a direct workbook citation.
